references.text: The description of the land flowing with milk and honey is first used by God when He promises to lead Israel out of Egypt into Canaan.
The promise of a land flowing with milk and honey is repeated as part of the covenant with Israel.
God reaffirms the promise of the land flowing with milk and honey.
The Lord describes the inheritance as a land flowing with milk and honey.
Moses reminds the people that the spies brought back fruit from the land as proof of its goodness.
The promise of the land flowing with milk and honey is linked to obedience to God.
The description of the promised land flowing with milk and honey in the confession of faith.
Israel asks for blessing over the land flowing with milk and honey.
Joshua confirms that the Lord brought the people into the land flowing with milk and honey.
Jeremiah refers to the land flowing with milk and honey in connection with the covenant.
Jeremiah reminds that God gave Israel the land flowing with milk and honey.
Ezekiel describes Canaan as the most glorious of all lands, flowing with milk and honey.
